blogPosts.title: Securing Web Applications: Best Practices for 2026
blogPosts.description: An essential checklist for developers and CTOs to defend modern web architectures against emerging client-side threats and security vulnerabilities.
blogPosts.author: Sahri Ramadan
blogPosts.content:
As we navigate 2026, the security landscape for web applications continues to shift at an unprecedented pace. The rise of advanced client-side vulnerabilities, third-party dependency compromises, and AI-powered phishing campaigns means traditional security boundaries are no longer sufficient to protect enterprise systems.

At Versa Morph, security is a core pillar of our software development cycle. Here are the crucial practices we implement across our client portfolios to guarantee robustness.

Prioritizing Content Security Policies (CSP)

Many developers treat CSP as an afterthought, but a strict CSP is one of the most effective tools to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. With modern frameworks generating dynamic code, developers must avoid 'unsafe-inline' and implement nonce-based CSPs to verify the integrity of executed scripts.

"Security is not a product or feature; it is a continuous process of verification and adaptation. Every dependency is a potential entry point.

Securing the Software Supply Chain

With npm packages receiving updates hourly, supply chain attacks have become a standard threat vector. We mandate automated dependency scanning (using tools like Snyk or GitHub Dependabot) and enforce lockfile immutability inside the CI/CD pipeline to prevent unauthorized package changes from slipping into production.

blogPosts.title: Building Scalable Micro-Frontends with Next.js 16
blogPosts.description: Exploring architecture strategies to scale massive frontends using Next.js 16, Module Federation, and monorepos.
blogPosts.author: Sahri Ramadan
blogPosts.content:
Micro-frontends have moved from a bleeding-edge architectural trend to a necessity for large corporate systems. As organizational teams grow, maintaining a single monolithic React application becomes counter-productive, resulting in merge conflicts, slow builds, and tight coupling.

Next.js 16 introduces refined support for modular builds and independent route modules, making micro-frontend architectures more stable and performant than ever.

The Power of Module Federation

Webpack Module Federation (and its modern successors) allows a Next.js application to dynamically load code from a completely different project at runtime. This means the checkout team can deploy updates to the checkout component without triggering a build or redeployment of the homepage or dashboard modules.

"Micro-frontends allow organizations to map their technical architectures directly to their business departments, accelerating feature delivery.

Shared Design Systems and Turborepo

To ensure a cohesive user experience across separate apps, we combine micro-frontends with a monorepo setup using Turborepo. Common UI components, utility functions, and configurations are packaged into a local design system workspace, which is consumed by individual applications with zero performance overhead during production builds.

blogPosts.title: The Power of Tailwind CSS v4 in Modern Web Design
blogPosts.description: An overview of the new CSS-first configuration and compiler engine in Tailwind v4, and how it accelerates frontend development.
blogPosts.author: Andika Noor Ismawan
blogPosts.content:
Tailwind CSS has dominated utility-first styling for years, but version 4 marks a fundamental rewrite of the tool. By ditching the traditional JavaScript-based configuration file in favor of a CSS-first setup, the framework achieves blazing-fast build speeds and simplified asset integration.

Our UX and engineering teams at Versa Morph have transitioned our base templates to Tailwind v4, resulting in a cleaner development workflow and faster project turnarounds.

CSS-First Configuration Engine

Instead of configuring theme colors and custom fonts inside tailwind.config.js, Tailwind v4 lets you customize your design tokens directly inside your CSS entrypoint using CSS custom properties. The compiler reads these properties and auto-generates corresponding utility classes at compile time, eliminating file duplication.

"Tailwind v4 returns style customization to where it belongs: CSS. The DX gains from compile-time optimizations are massive.

Performance Gains

The new Rust-based compiler engine compiles styles up to 10x faster than previous PostCSS implementations. For enterprise web platforms with thousands of dynamic routes and components, this means instantaneous hot module reloading (HMR) and a highly responsive developer experience.

blogPosts.title: Why Enterprise Mobile Apps Fail: Common UX Mistakes
blogPosts.description: Analyzing the UI/UX failures that drive employee and client abandonment in corporate mobile ecosystems and how to design for success.
blogPosts.author: Andika Noor Ismawan
blogPosts.content:
Enterprises invest millions in custom mobile apps to automate operations, track inventory, or boost sales engagement. Yet, a shocking percentage of these applications suffer from extremely low adoption rates, with employees and customers reverting to legacy web tools or spreadsheet workarounds.

At Versa Morph, we've audited and redesigned multiple enterprise systems. The root cause of abandonment is rarely bad code, it's almost always poor UX design.

The Overloaded Dashboard Trap

Many enterprise mobile apps try to pack an entire desktop dashboard into a 6-inch smartphone screen. This results in micro-text, cluttered layouts, and high cognitive load. Mobile UX design requires ruthless prioritization: identify the top three workflows users need on-the-go and make those workflows accessible within two taps.

"An enterprise app shouldn't be a feature-for-feature port of your desktop web system. It should be a hyper-focused utility.

Ignoring Offline Functionality

Logistics, warehouse, and field-sales employees often operate in spots with spotty cell coverage. If a mobile app crashes or freezes because it cannot access the server, users will immediately abandon it. Designing with an offline-first architecture, caching data locally and synchronizing seamlessly upon network recovery, is mandatory for enterprise adoption.

blogPosts.title: How to Build a High-Performance Team for Tech Startups
blogPosts.description: Strategies on cross-functional hiring, agile processes, and alignment to foster an elite engineering culture.
blogPosts.author: Andika Noor Ismawan
blogPosts.content:
Scaling a startup is a race against time, and your engineering team is the engine. However, many founders mistakenly believe that hiring more developers will automatically accelerate delivery. In reality, adding headcount without an established engineering culture often introduces communication overhead and slows down production.

Based on our experiences building and consulting for high-growth ventures, a highly optimized team structure outweighs pure headcount every time.

Cultivating a Cross-Functional Mindset

Siloing design, frontend, backend, and QA creates friction and slows feedback loops. High-performing teams are structured around independent product squads that contain all the skills necessary to ship a feature. This cross-functional alignment allows squads to take full ownership and iterate autonomously.

"When you build teams around business capabilities instead of technical stacks, you minimize handoffs and speed up shipping.

Focusing on Autonomy and Psychological Safety

An elite culture encourages developers to experiment and fail quickly. Enforcing rigid hierarchies and blaming engineers for production bugs leads to defensive coding and zero innovation. Establish automated test coverage and blameless post-mortems so the team feels safe deploying changes frequently.

blogPosts.title: Introduction to Serverless Architecture with AWS Lambda
blogPosts.description: Demystifying serverless compute, event-driven design, and how to scale backends with zero server maintenance.
blogPosts.author: Sahri Ramadan
blogPosts.content:
Serverless architecture has changed the economics of backend hosting. Traditionally, running an API required deploying a virtual server, configuring OS patches, and keeping a process running continuously even when there were no incoming requests. Serverless compute removes this operational overhead entirely.

At the heart of the AWS serverless catalog is AWS Lambda, which lets you execute code in response to specific system events with automatic scaling and sub-millisecond billing.

Event-Driven Execution Flow

Unlike traditional backend instances, a serverless function is completely stateless. It wakes up when triggered (e.g. an HTTP request via API Gateway, a database update, or a file upload to S3), processes the request, and spins down. Because you only pay for the execution time in milliseconds, organizations running intermittent or highly variable workloads can slash infrastructure costs by up to 90%.

"Serverless represents a shift in focus. Developers should spend their time writing business logic, not patching operating systems.

Designing for Statelessness

The core architectural shift is that serverless backends cannot rely on local in-memory storage for session state or long-running threads. Data must be persisted to external databases like DynamoDB or shared Redis clusters. While this requires a change in developer mindset, it ensures your system is infinitely scalable by design.

blogPosts.title: The Rise of Custom ERP Systems in Indonesian Logistics
blogPosts.description: Evaluating the operational benefits of custom ERP software over off-the-shelf platforms for Indonesia's growing supply chain sector.
blogPosts.author: Andika Noor Ismawan
blogPosts.content:
Indonesia's unique geography, an archipelago spanning thousands of islands, presents a complex logistics and supply chain environment. Off-the-shelf ERP platforms designed for contiguous landmasses frequently struggle to adapt to localized marine freight schedules, complex port regulations, and multi-tier distribution structures.

As logistics companies in Jakarta, Surabaya, and Medan scale, they are turning away from generic SaaS solutions and investing in custom-built ERP platforms designed for regional challenges.

Navigating Local Infrastructure Gaps

Custom ERP systems enable logistics providers to build deep integrations with local mapping APIs, customs databases, and regional third-party delivery networks. By mapping delivery routes that account for ferry schedules and local traffic restrictions, companies can reduce route delays and improve predictability.

"A generic ERP forces a business to bend its processes to fit the software. A custom ERP is designed to amplify the business's natural competitive advantage.

Real-Time Mobile Driver Integrations

Off-the-shelf enterprise platforms often feature expensive per-user licensing costs that make equipping thousands of field delivery drivers cost-prohibitive. A custom solution lets enterprises develop a tailored driver mobile app with zero seat licenses, streaming real-time geolocation updates directly back to the central dispatch desk.

blogPosts.title: Leveraging AI for Predictive Analytics in Smart Agriculture
blogPosts.description: How machine learning models are analyzing IoT telemetry to optimize crop yields and predict weather anomalies in Southeast Asia.
blogPosts.author: Sahri Ramadan
blogPosts.content:
The agriculture sector in Southeast Asia is facing extreme challenges from shifting weather patterns and soil nutrient depletion. Fortunately, the convergence of low-cost IoT soil sensors and predictive machine learning models offers a path toward sustainable, high-yield agriculture.

At Versa Morph, our IoT and AI engineering teams have designed systems that collect real-time data from palm oil and rice plantations, translating telemetry into predictive insights.

Translating Sensor Data to Insights

Traditional farming relies on historical schedules for watering and fertilization. By analyzing real-time soil moisture, nitrogen levels, and localized barometric data, our AI models can dynamically adjust irrigation schedules. The system predicts dry spells three days in advance, allowing farmers to optimize resources and protect crops.

"AI in agriculture is about moving from generalized schedules to hyper-personalized crop management.

Predicting Plant Disease Outbreaks

By feeding environmental humidity, leaf temperature, and historical crop disease datasets into classification models, agricultural organizations can predict pest or disease outbreaks before they spread. This localized early warning system allows target interventions, significantly reducing chemical pesticide usage.

blogPosts.title: How We Migrated to Next.js App Router: Lessons Learned
blogPosts.description: A developer-focused walkthrough detailing the migration from Pages Router to App Router, focusing on server components and state management.
blogPosts.author: Sahri Ramadan
blogPosts.content:
Next.js client-side rendering was revolutionized with the introduction of the App Router, but migrating a production application with hundreds of routes is a significant challenge. The mental shift from React Page routing to React Server Components (RSC) requires a fundamental rethink of data fetching and layout structure.

We recently migrated a large client's client portal to Next.js App Router. Here is what we learned during the transition.

RSC vs. Client Components

The most common mistake developers make during migration is slapping the 'use client' directive at the top of every file. To gain the performance benefits of Next.js, components should remain Server Components by default. Keep interactive elements like buttons, input fields, and custom animations localized within small leaf client components, while fetching data on the server.

"App Router migrations fail when teams try to replicate client-side routing patterns on server-first architectures.

Managing Shared State

Because server components do not support React Context directly, state management patterns must change. We utilize server routing queries and URL params as the single source of truth for UI state, supplemented by localized client context provider states where dynamic updates are mandatory. This design results in cleaner code and smaller client bundles.

blogPosts.title: Data Privacy Compliance in Indonesia: Navigating the UU PDP
blogPosts.description: An overview of Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP) and the technical measures enterprises must adopt to achieve compliance.
blogPosts.author: Andika Noor Ismawan
blogPosts.content:
Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Act (UU PDP) marks a historic turning point in how businesses collect, process, and secure user information. With strict penalties for non-compliance, companies can no longer rely on lax database access controls or simple click-wrap consent forms.

For businesses operating in the Indonesian market, understanding the technical implications of UU PDP compliance is essential to maintaining operations and brand trust.

Implementing Strict Consent Management

Under the UU PDP, consent must be explicitly given, verifiable, and easily revocable. This means web and mobile interfaces must replace pre-checked agreement boxes with clear, granular options. Additionally, backends must maintain auditable consent logs documenting when and how users agreed to data processing.

"Data privacy is no longer just a legal issue. It is a core feature of modern system design.

Securing Data at Rest and in Transit

Securing personal identifiable information (PII) requires database column-level encryption for sensitive fields, such as ID numbers (NIK) and phone numbers. Combined with robust Key Management Services (KMS) and access-control policies, this ensures that even in the event of a database dump, the underlying user data remains unreadable.

blogPosts.title: Optimizing API Performance: gRPC vs REST in 2026
blogPosts.description: Comparing payload efficiency, latency, and streaming capabilities between gRPC and REST for inter-service communication.
blogPosts.author: Sahri Ramadan
blogPosts.content:
As enterprise systems grow into dozens of microservices, the performance of inter-service APIs dictates overall system responsiveness. While REST over HTTP/1.1 remains the default standard for public-facing client integrations, its overhead makes it inefficient for high-frequency internal calls.

gRPC, built on HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers, offers a lightweight, strongly-typed alternative designed for low-latency communication.

Payload Size and Serialization

REST APIs typically rely on JSON, which is human-readable but text-heavy. In contrast, gRPC serializes data into a compact binary format using Protocol Buffers. In our internal benchmarks, switching from JSON to Protocol Buffers reduced payload sizes by 40-60%, resulting in immediate network bandwidth savings.

"By replacing internal REST calls with gRPC, we eliminated network bottlenecks and slashed microservice response times.

HTTP/2 and Multiplexing

Unlike HTTP/1.1, which requires opening a new TCP connection for every request or dealing with Head-of-Line blocking, gRPC utilizes HTTP/2 multiplexing. This allows multiple requests and responses to stream concurrently over a single connection, significantly reducing connection-establishment latencies.

blogPosts.title: A Guide to CI/CD Automation for Mobile Applications
blogPosts.description: Automating builds, testing, and deployment to Google Play Store and Apple App Store using Fastlane and CI pipelines.
blogPosts.author: Sahri Ramadan
blogPosts.content:
While web developers enjoy rapid deployments, mobile engineers face compilation times, code signing configurations, and app store review processes. Manually archiving builds, signing profiles, and uploading binaries to the App Store or Play Console eats up valuable development hours.

Implementing a structured CI/CD pipeline tailored for mobile applications automates these processes, allowing teams to deliver bug fixes with confidence.

Automating Signatures and Provisioning Profiles

Code signing is the bane of iOS development. We leverage Fastlane Match to manage iOS distribution certificates and provisioning profiles. Match stores all credentials in a private Git repository, decrypting them automatically in the CI runner during production archiving.

"Manual code signing is a major security risk and team bottleneck. Automating it keeps configurations consistent.

Integrating Cloud Runners and Testing

A robust pipeline runs unit and visual regression tests on virtual simulators before triggering a deployment. We utilize cloud runners like GitHub Actions or Codemagic, ensuring that only builds passing 100% of test scenarios are pushed to TestFlight or Google Play Beta tracks.

blogPosts.title: Designing for Accessibility: Inclusive Web Design Practices
blogPosts.description: How to build web interfaces that comply with WCAG 2.2 standards, ensuring your application is usable by everyone.
blogPosts.author: Andika Noor Ismawan
blogPosts.content:
Accessibility (a11y) is frequently mischaracterized as a legal checkmark rather than a core UX design discipline. In reality, building accessible interfaces benefits all users, improving readability on mobile screens, facilitating keyboard navigation, and driving SEO performance.

With the enforcement of the WCAG 2.2 standards, digital products must prioritize accessibility from initial Figma wireframes to final CSS code.

Semantic HTML and ARIA Guidelines

Relying solely on styled <div> and <span> elements for interactive controls breaks screen-reader parsing. UX engineers must utilize semantic tags like <main>, <nav>, and <button>, supplementing them with clear ARIA attributes when building complex components.

"Accessibility is not about building a separate version of your site. It is about coding the default version correctly.

Contrast Ratios and Interactive Sizing

Ensure text elements achieve a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 against their backgrounds (3:1 for large text). Furthermore, interactive elements like buttons and input selectors must maintain a minimum target size of 44x44 CSS pixels to avoid frustrating users on touch screens.

blogPosts.title: Scaling Databases: Sharding vs Replication Explained
blogPosts.description: A comprehensive guide to backend data scaling, comparing replication strategies and horizontal sharding.
blogPosts.author: Sahri Ramadan
blogPosts.content:
When scaling web applications, the database is almost always the first component to hit CPU or I/O performance bottlenecks. While scaling compute instances horizontally is trivial, scaling databases is a complex, stateful challenge.

Before jumping to complex horizontal sharding architectures, software architects must evaluate read-replica systems and their trade-offs.

Leveraging Read Replication

Replication involves copying database updates from a primary write-instance to multiple read-only instances. For applications with read-heavy patterns (e.g. blogs, e-commerce catalog browsing), offloading queries to read replicas can resolve performance issues with minimal code modifications.

"Replication scales reads easily. Sharding scales writes but introduces significant architectural complexity.

When to Transition to Sharding

When write transactions exhaust primary database capacity, sharding becomes necessary. Sharding partitions data horizontally across separate physical servers based on a shard key (e.g., customer country or tenant ID). While sharding offers infinite write scale, it complicates join queries and transaction rollbacks.

blogPosts.title: The Role of Digital Transformation in Post-Pandemic Retail
blogPosts.description: How modern retail brands are integrating e-commerce platforms with omnichannel POS systems to deliver unified customer journeys.
blogPosts.author: Andika Noor Ismawan
blogPosts.content:
The retail industry has undergone a permanent structural shift. Consumers no longer distinguish between offline and online shopping channels; they expect a seamless, unified interaction whether browsing on a mobile phone or speaking with a store clerk.

At Versa Morph, we've helped brick-and-mortar retail brands build digital architectures that bridge the physical and digital divide.

Connecting POS and E-Commerce Databases

The core blocker to omnichannel success is siloed stock data. If a customer buys the last item online while a physical shopper takes it off the shelf, it leads to cancelled orders and bad reviews. Real-time synchronization between in-store POS terminals and cloud e-commerce databases is the foundational step of digital retail transformation.

"Omnichannel is not about being present on every platform. It is about syncing data so the customer sees one unified brand.

Enabling Buy Online, Pick Up In-Store (BOPIS)

BOPIS workflows require real-time stock allocation and automated notification pipelines. When an online order comes in, the local store team is instantly notified to prepare the package. This approach increases foot traffic to physical stores while meeting consumers' demands for speed.

blogPosts.title: Building a Collaborative Remote Engineering Culture
blogPosts.description: Key lessons on asynchronous communication, documentation, and tooling to align distributed engineering teams.
blogPosts.author: Andika Noor Ismawan
blogPosts.content:
Remote work offers access to a global talent pool, but running a remote engineering team is not as simple as setting up a Slack workspace. Without structured guidelines, communication breakdowns lead to duplicate work and misaligned team members.

At Versa Morph, our team operates distributedly across multiple regions. Here is how we maintain cohesion and deliver high-quality code.

Embracing Asynchronous Communication

Mandating real-time responses to chat messages ruins developers' deep work blocks. We design team workflows around asynchronous communication: detailed pull requests, comprehensive design documents, and recorded screen demonstrations. This allows developers to focus on writing code, catching up on updates during their scheduled breaks.

"Writing down technical specs and documentation is a force multiplier for remote organizations.

Establishing a Single Source of Truth

When project specifications are scattered across Slack threads, Jira tickets, and comments in Google Docs, mistakes happen. We enforce keeping all project specifications inside the Git repository's markdown files. This ensures that every developer is working off the same roadmap.

projects.title: AI-Powered Patient Monitoring Ecosystem
projects.description: We designed and built an end-to-end AI patient monitoring ecosystem spanning multiple ICU divisions, combining edge AI inference with cloud-based predictive analytics. The system continuously processes high-frequency vital sign telemetry to detect early signs of clinical deterioration, replacing legacy threshold-based alerting with context-aware intelligence. From firmware-level data acquisition on bedside monitors to a clinician-facing dashboard and mobile alerting system, the entire stack was engineered for sub-second response in critical care environments.
projects.problem: Traditional threshold-based monitoring in ICU wards suffered from a 40% false negative rate, meaning nearly half of genuine deterioration events went undetected until they escalated into critical emergencies. Nurses were overwhelmed by alert fatigue from excessive false positives, while true deterioration signals were buried in noise. The existing system provided no trend analysis, no predictive capability, and no integration with historical patient records. Preventable adverse events were rising, mortality risk was increasing, and the hospital faced mounting regulatory scrutiny.
projects.solution: Versa Morph deployed a hybrid edge-cloud architecture purpose-built for clinical environments. Each bedside monitor runs a lightweight TensorFlow Lite anomaly detection model locally, achieving sub-100ms inference latency on edge hardware. Aggregated telemetry feeds into a central transformer-based model in the cloud that learns population-level deterioration patterns across thousands of patient histories. The pipeline ingests 200+ data points per second including heart rate variability, oxygen saturation trends, blood pressure dynamics, respiratory rate, and medication history. A React-based clinician dashboard provides real-time visualization with configurable alert thresholds, while a dedicated mobile app ensures critical alerts reach on-call staff within seconds.
projects.result: False negative rate dropped from 40% to 3%. The system delivers an average 45-minute early warning before critical events, giving clinical teams a crucial intervention window. ICU mortality decreased by 28% within the first six months. Alert fatigue was reduced by 60% through intelligent suppression of non-actionable notifications. The platform now processes over 50 million data points daily across all monitored wards and has become the foundation for the hospital's clinical decision support strategy.

Equipment failures caused an average of 200 hours of unplanned downtime per year, translating to Rp65 Miliar in lost production. Maintenance was entirely reactive: machines ran until they failed, then emergency repairs halted entire production lines. Centralized cloud processing was ruled out due to sub-5ms latency requirements for critical vibration analysis and intermittent factory floor connectivity. Each node runs a highly optimized Go-based data ingestion pipeline that processes raw sensor streams locally using lightweight anomaly detection models. Only critical alerts and daily aggregates are transmitted to a central Vue.js operations dashboard via MQTT with store-and-forward capability for unreliable networks. The system includes over-the-air firmware updates, health monitoring for every edge node, and a centralized configuration management system. A Grafana-based analytics layer provides historical trend analysis and failure pattern recognition across all facilities.
projects.result: Alert latency dropped to sub-10ms at the edge, enabling real-time machine health monitoring. Unplanned downtime decreased by 67% across all 12 factories, saving Rp43 Miliar annually in avoided production losses. Predictive maintenance scheduling replaced reactive repairs, extending average machine lifespan by 18%. projects.problem: A 25-year-old mainframe-based core banking system was consuming Rp186 Miliar annually in maintenance costs while delivering diminishing returns. Transaction processing peaked at 500 TPS, causing visible slowdowns during payroll cycles and holiday periods. New feature deployment required 6-9 months due to deep monolithic coupling: a change to the interest calculation module could break the customer onboarding flow. The system had no API layer, no real-time fraud detection, and no mobile banking capability. The bank was losing competitive ground to fintech entrants while bearing among the highest infrastructure costs in the industry.

A Next.js admin panel provides bank staff with real-time transaction monitoring, customer management, and regulatory reporting. The customer-facing mobile app was rebuilt from scratch with React Native, featuring biometric authentication, real-time notifications, and a modern UI. The migration followed a strangler fig pattern, routing traffic through an API gateway that gradually shifted load from legacy to new services over a 6-month period.

projects.title: Real-time Supply Chain Analytics Dashboard
projects.description: We built a real-time supply chain visibility platform that transforms raw fleet telemetry into actionable intelligence. The system unifies GPS tracking, fuel consumption analytics, route optimization, and predictive maintenance into a single operational dashboard, replacing manual dispatch processes with data-driven decision-making. From IoT sensor integration on 500+ vehicles to a custom Apache Kafka streaming pipeline and PowerBI executive dashboards, the platform provides end-to-end visibility across the entire delivery network.
projects.problem: A fleet of 500+ delivery vehicles operated with manual routing, paper-based dispatch, and zero real-time visibility into vehicle locations, fuel usage, or driver behavior. Customer delivery SLA compliance had fallen to 85%, with no way to identify bottlenecks or predict delays before they occurred. Fuel costs were 20% above industry benchmarks due to inefficient routing and no visibility into idling or deviations. Maintenance was reactive: vehicles broke down mid-route, causing cascading delays across the network. Executive reporting required manual data aggregation from spreadsheets, taking days to produce insights that were already stale.
projects.solution: Versa Morph designed a modern data stack purpose-built for logistics intelligence. IoT sensors installed on each vehicle stream GPS coordinates, fuel consumption, engine diagnostics, and driver behavior metrics via cellular connectivity to Google Cloud. Apache Kafka handles real-time event ingestion at 10,000+ events per minute, while dbt transformations clean and model the data for analytics. A custom ML pipeline predicts optimal delivery routes based on traffic patterns, weather data, and historical delivery times. PowerBI dashboards provide executives with real-time fleet health, SLA compliance, and cost analysis. A React-based dispatch panel gives operations managers live vehicle tracking with 30-second refresh intervals and automated route reassignment when delays are detected.

projects.title: Omnichannel POS & Loyalty App
projects.description: We developed a full-stack omnichannel retail platform that unifies in-store POS terminals, e-commerce inventory, and a digital loyalty engine into a single real-time ecosystem. The system eliminates stockout blind spots by synchronizing inventory across 200+ physical locations and online channels, while a custom loyalty engine drives cross-channel revenue through personalized promotions and purchase history analytics. From Flutter-based POS applications running on Android tablets to a Laravel backend with real-time inventory synchronization, the platform bridges the gap between physical and digital retail.
projects.problem: 200+ retail stores operated independent POS systems with no integration to the e-commerce platform. Inventory was tracked separately at each location, creating blind spots where online orders could be fulfilled from stock that was already sold in-store. Customer loyalty was managed through physical punch cards that provided no data insights and had a 70% loss rate. Stockout rates reached 15% due to inventory discrepancies between channels, directly impacting revenue and customer satisfaction. The lack of unified customer data meant no personalized marketing, no cross-channel promotions, and no visibility into purchasing patterns across the entire retail network.
projects.solution: Versa Morph built a Flutter-based POS application that runs on Android tablets across all 200+ locations, connected to a Laravel backend with a shared PostgreSQL database serving as the single source of truth for inventory. Real-time stock synchronization ensures that when an item sells in-store, the e-commerce platform updates within 2 seconds. A custom loyalty engine captures every transaction across all channels, building rich customer profiles that power personalized push notifications, targeted promotions, and tiered reward programs. projects.title: Smart Agriculture IoT Monitoring Platform

projects.problem: Over 10,000 hectares of farmland across multiple regions operated with zero real-time environmental monitoring. Farmers relied on manual soil inspections and experience-based intuition to manage irrigation, leading to 25% water wastage through over-watering and crop stress from under-watering. No historical soil data existed to identify patterns or optimize practices across seasons. Weather data was available but not integrated with field-level conditions, making it impossible to adjust irrigation based on actual soil moisture. The lack of data made it difficult to scale operations, train new farm managers, or demonstrate sustainable practices to regulators.
projects.solution: Versa Morph deployed a LoRaWAN-based sensor network with 2,000+ battery-powered nodes distributed across all 10,000+ hectares. Each node measures soil moisture at three depths, soil pH, ambient temperature, humidity, and light intensity, transmitting data every 15 minutes through a mesh network of 40 LoRaWAN gateways to a central AWS IoT Core backend. An ML pipeline built with Python and TensorFlow processes sensor data alongside weather forecasts and historical crop yields to generate field-specific irrigation recommendations. A Grafana dashboard provides agronomists with real-time visualization of soil conditions, moisture trends, and irrigation schedules. A Flutter-based mobile app delivers irrigation alerts and recommendations directly to farm managers in the field, working offline with sync-when-connected capability for areas with limited connectivity.
projects.result: Water consumption decreased by 30% across all monitored hectares through precision irrigation scheduling. Crop yield increased by 22% in the first full growing season. The platform identified three previously undetected drainage issues that were causing chronic crop stress in specific zones. The platform includes a mobile-first PWA with offline content caching, a discussion forum with AI-powered moderation, and automated assessment with plagiarism detection. projects.result: Successfully onboarded 100,000+ concurrent students with 99.99% uptime during peak exam periods. projects.title: Secure Digital ID Infrastructure Migration
projects.description: We led a zero-trust digital identity infrastructure migration for 50M+ citizen records, moving from a legacy on-premise Oracle database to a modern, geo-redundant AWS architecture. The project encompassed security architecture design, data pipeline engineering, phased migration execution, and post-migration validation across a 6-month engagement. Every step was designed for zero downtime and zero data loss, with a comprehensive rollback strategy tested through 5 full rehearsal runs before the final production cutover.
projects.problem: A government agency managing 50M+ citizen digital identities was operating on a legacy Oracle database hosted on aging on-premise infrastructure. The system had suffered two security breaches in the prior year, exposing vulnerability gaps that the existing architecture could not address. The database could not scale to support new e-government services, with peak query times exceeding 30 seconds during high-demand periods. Disaster recovery relied on tape backups with a 48-hour restoration window. The agency needed to migrate to a modern, geo-redundant AWS infrastructure while maintaining 100% data integrity and zero service interruption for citizens relying on digital identity services.
projects.solution: Versa Morph designed a zero-trust security architecture using AWS WAF, Shield Advanced, and KMS for encryption at rest and in transit. Every service-to-service communication is authenticated via mTLS, and all data access is logged to a centralized SIEM. The migration followed a phased approach: Go-based data pipelines extract, transform, and load records with checksum verification at every step, comparing source and destination hashes to ensure byte-level accuracy. A comprehensive rollback plan was tested across 5 full rehearsal migrations, each processing millions of records to validate the pipeline under production-like load. The final cutover was executed over a single maintenance weekend using a blue-green deployment strategy, with traffic gradually shifted from legacy to new infrastructure while real-time monitoring confirmed data consistency.
projects.result: All 50M+ citizen identities migrated with zero data loss and zero downtime. Security incident response time decreased from 48 hours to 15 minutes through automated threat detection and response playbooks. The platform achieved FedRAMP High equivalent certification. Query performance improved from 30+ seconds to sub-200ms. Disaster recovery restoration window dropped from 48 hours to 15 minutes with automated failover. The migration enabled 12 new e-government services that were previously impossible due to infrastructure limitations. The project has been cited as a benchmark for government infrastructure modernization.

We use **API gateways**, **message queues** (Kafka, RabbitMQ), and **ETL pipelines** (Airbyte, Fivetran) to ensure seamless data flow.

faqItems.question: How do you ensure data security?
faqItems.answer:
Security is embedded in every phase of our development:

- **Zero-Trust Architecture**: No implicit trust, continuous verification
- **Encryption**: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit
- **Cloud security**: SOC 2 compliant infrastructure
- **Code security**: Regular SAST/DAST scanning, dependency audits
- **Access control**: RBAC, MFA, and audit logging
- **Compliance**: GDPR, CCPA, Indonesia's UU PDP, and ISO 27001 frameworks

We also conduct **quarterly penetration tests** by third-party security firms.

faqItems.question: Do you provide code ownership and documentation?
faqItems.answer:
Yes, **you own 100% of the code, IP, and deliverables** from day one. We provide:

- Full source code in your private repository
- Technical architecture documentation (ADR)
- API documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger)
- Deployment and runbook guides
- Admin and user manuals

There are no lock-ins, license fees, or proprietary dependencies.

faqItems.question: How do you handle legacy technology?
faqItems.answer:
We have extensive experience with legacy systems:

- **Assessment**: Audit current systems for technical debt and migration feasibility
- **Strangler Fig pattern**: Incrementally replace legacy components
- **API wrapping**: Expose legacy functionality through modern APIs
- **Data migration**: ETL pipelines with rollback capability
- **Coexistence strategy**: Run old and new systems in parallel during transition

We've modernized systems written in COBOL, VB6, Delphi, and legacy PHP frameworks.

faqItems.question: What is your approach to testing?
faqItems.answer:
We follow a **multi-layer testing strategy**:

1. **Unit tests**: Jest, Vitest, Go testing (80%+ coverage target)
2. **Integration tests**: API contract tests, database migrations
3. **E2E tests**: Playwright / Cypress for critical user flows
4. **Performance tests**: k6 / Locust for load and stress testing
5. **Security tests**: SAST (SonarQube), DAST (OWASP ZAP)
6. **Accessibility tests**: axe-core, Lighthouse, manual screen reader testing

Tests run automatically in CI/CD pipelines. No pull request merges without passing checks.

faqItems.question: Do you offer post-launch support?
faqItems.answer:
Yes. We offer comprehensive post-launch support through our **Managed Services** program:

- **Bug fixes & hotfixes**: Critical issue resolution within 4 hours
- **Performance monitoring**: 24/7 infrastructure and application monitoring
- **Security patches**: Regular vulnerability assessments and updates
- **Feature enhancements**: Ongoing improvements based on user feedback
- **24/7 incident response**: For critical production systems

Custom [SLA](/sla) packages are available to match your business needs.

faqItems.question: What is your typical response time for support?
faqItems.answer:
Our support response times are tied to severity levels:

| Severity | Response Time | Target Resolution |
|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| **Critical** (system down) | ≤ 1 hour | ≤ 4 hours |
| **High** (major feature broken) | ≤ 4 hours | ≤ 24 hours |
| **Medium** (minor issue) | ≤ 8 hours | ≤ 48 hours |
| **Low** (cosmetic / question) | ≤ 24 hours | ≤ 5 business days |

All support tiers include 24/7 ticket submission via our portal.

faqItems.question: Can you scale a team up or down quickly?
faqItems.answer:
Yes. Our **elastic team model** is designed for flexibility:

- **Scale up**: Add engineers, designers, or PMs within 1-2 weeks
- **Scale down**: Reduce team size with 2-week notice
- **Swap roles**: Replace specialists as project phases change

This means you pay only for what you need, when you need it. Ideal for startups and enterprises alike.

faqItems.question: Do you provide training for our internal team?
faqItems.answer:
Yes. We offer **knowledge transfer and training** as part of our engagements:

- **Code walkthroughs**: Regular sessions explaining architecture and implementation
- **Pair programming**: Work alongside your developers to build capability
- **Workshops**: Technology-specific training (React, cloud, CI/CD, etc.)
- **Documentation**: Comprehensive runbooks and operational guides
- **Shadow support**: Your team shadows ours during the first month post-launch

Our goal is to make your team self-sufficient, not dependent on us.

faqItems.question: What happens after the project ends?
faqItems.answer:
We offer multiple transition options:

1. **Full handover**: Complete knowledge transfer, documentation, and training
2. **Managed support**: Ongoing maintenance and support via SLA
3. **Hybrid**: Your team takes over daily operations, we handle complex issues
4. **Extended development**: Continue with new features and enhancements

There's no hard stop. We work with you to find the transition model that fits your team's readiness and budget.

faqItems.question: Do you offer emergency support for systems you didn't build?
faqItems.answer:
Yes. We provide **emergency incident response** for any system, even if we didn't build it:

- **Critical outage**: 1-hour response, 4-hour resolution target
- **Security incident**: Immediate containment and forensic analysis
- **Performance degradation**: Root cause analysis and remediation

This is available through our **Incident Response Retainer**. Pay a monthly fee for guaranteed priority access to our senior engineers.

legalPages.title: Privacy Policy
legalPages.subtitle: This Privacy Policy describes how Versa Morph collects, processes, stores, and protects your personal data. It applies to all visitors, users, and clients of our website, platforms, and services.
legalPages.content:
1. Scope & Controller Identity

This Privacy Policy governs the processing of personal data by Versa Morph, a company established under the laws of the Republic of Indonesia with its registered office at Jl. M.H. Thamrin No. 1, Jakarta Pusat, DKI Jakarta 10310, Indonesia. Versa Morph acts as the data controller with respect to personal data collected through its website, platforms, and services, unless otherwise specified in a separate Data Processing Agreement.

This Policy applies to all processing activities carried out by Versa Morph, including but not limited to: (a) browsing and interacting with our website; (b) registering for or using our software, IoT, and infrastructure services; (c) communicating with our sales, support, or engineering teams; and (d) subscribing to our marketing and newsletter communications.

2. Data We Collect

We collect and process the following categories of personal data, depending on the nature of our engagement:

2.1 Information You Provide Voluntarily

  • —Identity Data: Full name, job title, company name, and professional affiliation.
  • —Contact Data: Email address, phone number, and billing or correspondence address.
  • —Account Data: Username, password (stored as a salted hash), API keys, and authentication credentials.
  • —Financial Data: Invoice details, payment method information, and transaction history (processed via PCI-DSS compliant payment processors).
  • —Communications: Records of correspondence with our sales, support, and engineering teams, including call recordings where permitted by law.

2.2 Information Collected Automatically

  • —Technical Data: IP address, browser type and version, time zone setting, browser plug-in types and versions, operating system and platform, device identifiers, and hardware telemetry from IoT sensors.
  • —Usage Data: Information about how you interact with our website and services, including pages visited, clickstream data, session duration, feature usage, and error reports.
  • —Cookie Data: Data collected via cookies and similar tracking technologies, as described in our Cookie Policy.

2.3 Information from Third Parties

We may receive personal data about you from third-party sources, including: (a) business partners and resellers; (b) publicly available databases and professional networks (e.g., LinkedIn); (c) credit reference and fraud prevention agencies; and (d) analytics providers (e.g., Vercel Analytics).

3. Legal Basis for Processing

We process your personal data only where we have a valid legal basis under applicable data protection law (including the GDPR, UK GDPR, and CCPA/CPRA). The legal bases we rely on are:

  • —Performance of a Contract (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)): Where processing is necessary to provide our services, fulfill our obligations under a Master Service Agreement, or take pre-contractual steps at your request.
  • —Consent (GDPR Art. 6(1)(a)): Where you have freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous consent, such as for marketing communications, non-essential cookies, and optional data processing activities. You may withdraw consent at any time.
  • —Legitimate Interests (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)): Where processing is necessary for our legitimate business interests, provided those interests do not override your fundamental rights and freedoms. Our legitimate interests include improving our services, ensuring network and information security, and direct marketing to existing clients.
  • —Legal Obligation (GDPR Art. 6(1)(c)): Where processing is necessary to comply with a legal or regulatory obligation to which we are subject, including tax, anti-money laundering, and data breach notification laws.

4. Purposes of Processing

We process personal data for the following purposes:

  • —Service Delivery: Provisioning, maintaining, and improving our software, IoT infrastructure, and enterprise solutions, including technical support and incident resolution.
  • —Communications: Responding to inquiries, sending service-related notices (security alerts, scheduled maintenance, terms updates), and transactional communications.
  • —Analytics & Optimization: Analyzing usage patterns, telemetry data, and system performance metrics to enhance functionality, reliability, and user experience.
  • —Legal Compliance: Fulfilling obligations under applicable laws and regulations, including data subject rights requests, tax reporting, and regulatory disclosures.
  • —Marketing (with consent): Sending newsletters, event invitations, and product updates where you have opted in to receive such communications.

Versa Morph does not sell personal data to third parties. We do not engage in automated decision-making or profiling that produces legal effects concerning you, unless explicitly disclosed and consented to in advance.

5. Data Retention

We retain personal data only for as long as necessary to fulfil the purposes for which it was collected, including to satisfy any legal, accounting, or reporting requirements. The retention periods are as follows:

  • —Account and Client Data: Retained for the duration of the contractual relationship plus seven (7) years thereafter to comply with tax and commercial law obligations.
  • —Marketing Data: Retained until you withdraw consent or unsubscribe, or after two (2) years of inactivity, whichever occurs first.
  • —Technical Logs: IP addresses and server logs retained for a maximum of twelve (12) months, after which they are anonymized or deleted.
  • —IoT Telemetry Data: Retained per the terms of the applicable Statement of Work, not to exceed the contractual term plus six (6) months unless otherwise agreed.

When retention periods expire, personal data is securely deleted or anonymized such that it can no longer be attributed to an identifiable individual.

6. Security Measures

Versa Morph implements a comprehensive information security program incorporating administrative, technical, and physical safeguards commensurate with the sensitivity of the personal data we process. These measures include:

  • —Encryption: Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.3. Access to encryption keys is restricted via a hardware security module (HSM) and key management policy.
  • —Access Controls: Role-based access control (RBAC), multi-factor authentication (MFA), and the principle of least privilege are enforced across all systems. Access rights are reviewed quarterly.
  • —Network Security: Zero Trust architecture with micro-segmentation, web application firewall (WAF), DDoS mitigation, intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS), and 24/7 security operations center (SOC) monitoring.
  • —Vulnerability Management: Automated vulnerability scanning (weekly), third-party penetration testing (annually), and a formal patch management process with defined SLAs for critical vulnerabilities.
  • —Personnel: All employees and contractors undergo mandatory annual security and privacy training. Access to personal data is logged and audited.

While no system can guarantee absolute security, our cloud environments are designed to align with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 control frameworks, and our infrastructure undergoes independent security assessments on an annual basis.

7. Data Sharing & Third Parties

We do not sell your personal data. We may share personal data with the following categories of recipients, and only where a lawful basis exists:

  • —Subprocessors: Cloud infrastructure providers (AWS, Google Cloud, Vercel), data analytics services, and communication platforms, all bound by written data processing agreements consistent with this Policy.
  • —Professional Advisors: Lawyers, auditors, and insurers where necessary to establish, exercise, or defend legal rights.
  • —Regulatory Authorities: Data protection authorities, tax authorities, law enforcement, or other government bodies where we are legally required to do so.
  • —Business Transfers: In the event of a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of our assets, personal data may be transferred to the acquiring entity, subject to confidentiality obligations and continued compliance with this Policy.

8. International Data Transfers

Versa Morph is based in Indonesia and processes data primarily in the Asia Pacific region. Where we transfer personal data to countries that have not been deemed adequate by the European Commission or other competent authorities, we implement appropriate safeguards, including:

  • —Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as adopted by the European Commission and the UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO).
  • —Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs), where applicable.
  • —Data Processing Agreements incorporating the applicable Standard Contractual Clauses.
  • —Verification that the recipient is certified under an approved mechanism such as the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or its successor.

You may request a copy of the safeguards we have implemented for international transfers by contacting our DPO at the contact details in Section 12.

9. Your Rights

Depending on your jurisdiction, you may have the following rights under applicable data protection law (including the GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law / UU PDP):

  • —Right of Access: You may request confirmation of whether we process your personal data and, if so, access to that data along with information about the processing.
  • —Right to Rectification: You may request the correction of inaccurate or incomplete personal data.
  • —Right to Erasure ("Right to be Forgotten"): You may request deletion of your personal data where there is no compelling legal basis for continued processing.
  • —Right to Restriction: You may request restriction of processing in certain circumstances, such as where you contest the accuracy of the data.
  • —Right to Data Portability: You may request a copy of your personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and have it transmitted to another controller.
  • —Right to Object: You may object to processing based on legitimate interests, including profiling and direct marketing. We will cease processing unless we demonstrate compelling legitimate grounds.
  • —Right to Withdraw Consent: Where processing is based on consent, you may withdraw that consent at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal.
  • —Right to Lodge a Complaint: You have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority if you believe your rights have been infringed.

To exercise any of these rights, please contact us using the details in Section 12. We will respond to your request within thirty (30) days, or such shorter period as required by applicable law. We may request proof of identity before processing your request.

10. Children's Privacy

Our services are not directed to individuals under the age of sixteen (16). We do not knowingly collect personal data from children. If we become aware that a child under 16 has provided us with personal data, we will take steps to delete such information promptly. If you believe we have inadvertently collected data from a child, please contact us immediately.

11. Changes to This Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our data processing practices, legal obligations, or technological landscape. When we make material changes, we will notify you by email (if we have your contact information) or by posting a prominent notice on our website prior to the change becoming effective. We encourage you to review this Policy periodically. The "Last Updated" date at the top of this page indicates when this Policy was last revised.

12. Contact & Data Protection Officer

If you have any questions, concerns, or requests regarding this Privacy Policy or our data processing practices, or if you wish to exercise any of your data protection rights, please contact:

legalPages.title: Cookie Policy
legalPages.subtitle: This Cookie Policy explains how Versa Morph uses cookies, web beacons, and similar tracking technologies on our website and digital platforms. It forms part of our Privacy Policy and should be read in conjunction with it.
legalPages.content:
1. Introduction

Versa Morph (“we,” “us,” or “our”) uses cookies and similar tracking technologies on our website at https://versamorph.id (the “Site”) and our digital platforms. This Cookie Policy explains what cookies are, how we use them, the types of cookies we set, your rights to control and manage cookies, and the legal basis for our use of cookies.

This policy should be read together with our Privacy Policy, which provides more detailed information about how we process personal data.

2. What Are Cookies

Cookies are small text files (typically consisting of letters and numbers) that are stored on your browser or device (computer, tablet, or mobile) when you visit a website. Cookies are widely used to make websites function properly, enhance user experience, and provide information to the website owners about how their site is used.

Cookies can be categorized by their lifespan:

  • —Session Cookies: These are temporary cookies that expire when you close your browser. They enable the Site to remember your actions during a single browsing session.
  • —Persistent Cookies: These remain on your device until they expire (according to their set expiration date) or until you delete them. They enable the Site to remember your preferences and settings across browsing sessions.

Cookies can also be categorized by their origin:

  • —First-Party Cookies: Set directly by the website you are visiting (i.e., by Versa Morph).
  • —Third-Party Cookies: Set by a domain other than the one you are visiting, typically by external services or analytics providers.

In addition to cookies, we may use other similar tracking technologies such as web beacons (small transparent image files, also known as “pixel tags” or “clear GIFs”), local storage, and device fingerprinting technologies for the purposes described in this policy.

3. Cookies We Use

Versa Morph uses the following categories of cookies on our Site. We conduct periodic cookie audits to ensure the accuracy of this information.

Category Purpose Examples Duration
Strictly Essential Required for the basic functionality of the Site, including page navigation, secure area access, and load balancing. These cannot be disabled. cookie-consent, PHPSESSID, XSRF-TOKEN Session / Persistent
Functional / Preference Remember your preferences (language, region, theme, font size) to provide an enhanced, personalized experience. lang, theme Up to 1 year
Analytics / Performance Help us understand how visitors interact with our Site by collecting anonymized, aggregated data (pages visited, time spent, error rates, click patterns). We use this data to improve our Site and services. _vp_* (Vercel Analytics) Up to 2 years

4. Third-Party Cookies

In addition to the cookies we set directly (first-party cookies), the following third-party services may set their own cookies when you use our Site. These third parties have各自的 privacy policies governing their use of cookies:

  • —Vercel Analytics: Anonymous, privacy-preserving traffic analysis to understand website performance and usage patterns. Vercel Analytics does not use cross-site tracking and does not share data with advertising platforms. Vercel Privacy Policy
  • —Google Fonts: Font files are self-hosted where technically feasible. Where self-hosting is not possible, Google Fonts servers may log IP addresses and set cookies as described in Google's Privacy Policy.

We do not use advertising, targeting, or marketing cookies. We do not sell your browsing data to third parties. We do not use cookies for cross-context behavioral advertising.

5. Consent Management

When you first visit our Site, a cookie consent banner is displayed that allows you to:

  • —Accept All: Consents to the use of all categories of cookies, including functional and analytics cookies.
  • —Reject All: Consents only to strictly essential cookies. Functional and analytics cookies will not be set.
  • —Customize (where available): Select specific categories of cookies you wish to enable or disable.

Your consent is stored in a cookie on your device so that we can remember your preferences on subsequent visits. If you clear your cookies, the consent banner will reappear, and you will be asked to provide your preferences again. You may withdraw or change your consent at any time by clicking the “Cookie Preferences” link in the footer of our Site.

We record your consent as required by applicable law. Records of consent may include your IP address, the date and time of consent, the categories of cookies consented to, and the user agent string of your browser.

6. Managing & Deleting Cookies

In addition to the consent management mechanism described in Section 5, you can manage and delete cookies through your browser settings. Most browsers allow you to:

  • —View the cookies stored on your device and delete them individually or in bulk.
  • —Block cookies from specific domains or all cookies by default.
  • —Set preferences for cookies before they are set.
  • —Enable a “Do Not Track” (DNT) signal (though note that the Site does not currently respond to DNT signals given the lack of an industry-standard interpretation).

Instructions for managing cookies in common browsers:

  • —Google Chrome: Settings → Privacy and Security → Cookies and other site data.
  • —Mozilla Firefox: Options → Privacy & Security → Cookies and Site Data.
  • —Apple Safari: Preferences → Privacy → Cookies and website data.
  • —Microsoft Edge: Settings → Cookies and site permissions → Cookies and site data.

Please note that strictly essential cookies cannot be disabled through our consent management tool, as they are necessary for the Site to function. Disabling all cookies through your browser settings may affect the functionality and performance of our Site and other websites you visit.

7. Legal Basis

We process cookie data based on the following legal grounds under applicable data protection law:

  • —Strictly Essential Cookies: These cookies are necessary for the performance of our service (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b); ePrivacy Directive Art. 5(3) exception). They do not require prior consent.
  • —Functional & Analytics Cookies: These cookies are set based on your prior consent (GDPR Art. 6(1)(a); ePrivacy Directive Art. 5(3)). You provide consent via our cookie consent banner and may withdraw consent at any time by updating your preferences through the “Cookie Preferences” link in the footer of our Site. Withdrawal of consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal.

Where we rely on consent as the legal basis, we obtain your consent before any non-essential cookies are placed on your device. We ensure that your consent is freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, and revocable, in accordance with the requirements of the GDPR and the ePrivacy Directive.

8. California Rights (CCPA/CPRA)

If you are a resident of the State of California, the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (collectively, “CCPA”), provides you with additional rights regarding your personal information.

Versa Morph does not sell personal information as defined under the CCPA. In the preceding twelve (12) months, we have not sold any personal information of California residents. We do not share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising.

California residents have the right to: (a) request disclosure of the categories and specific pieces of personal information we have collected about you; (b) request deletion of personal information we have collected, subject to certain exceptions; (c) opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information (though we do not engage in such activities); and (d) not receive discriminatory treatment for exercising any of your CCPA rights. To exercise any of these rights, please contact us using the details in Section 10.

9. Policy Updates

We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time to reflect changes in technology, applicable regulations, our use of cookies, or our business practices. When we make material changes, we will update the “Last Updated” date at the top of this page and may notify you by email (if we have your contact information) or by posting a prominent notice on our Site.

We encourage you to review this Cookie Policy periodically to stay informed about how we use cookies and similar technologies. Your continued use of our Site following any changes to this policy constitutes acceptance of those changes, where such acceptance is required by law, we will obtain your prior consent.

10. Contact Us

If you have any questions, concerns, or requests regarding this Cookie Policy or our use of cookies and similar technologies, please contact:

  • —Data Protection Officer: dpo@versamorph.id
  • —General Inquiries: hello@versamorph.id
  • —Registered Address: Jl. M.H. Thamrin No. 1, Jakarta Pusat, DKI Jakarta 10310, Indonesia

legalPages.subtitle: This Service Level Agreement (“SLA”) governs the performance, availability, and reliability commitments applicable to Versa Morph's cloud-hosted production services. It is incorporated by reference into the Master Service Agreement between Versa Morph and the Client.
legalPages.content:
1. Scope & Purpose

This Service Level Agreement (“SLA”) sets forth the service level commitments, performance guarantees, support response times, and remedies available to clients (“Client” or “you”) of Versa Morph (“we,” “us,” or “our”). This SLA applies solely to cloud-hosted production services explicitly designated as “covered services” in the applicable Order Form, Master Service Agreement (“MSA”), or Statement of Work (“SOW”).

This SLA does not apply to: (a) free or trial services; (b) alpha, beta, or pre-release features explicitly labeled as “non-production”; (c) on-premise or client-managed deployments; (d) third-party services, applications, or data not under our control; or (e) services designated as “development” or “staging” unless expressly covered by a separate SOW. This SLA is incorporated by reference into the MSA. In the event of any conflict between this SLA and the MSA, the terms of the MSA shall prevail with respect to such conflict.

2. Definitions

For the purposes of this SLA, the following capitalized terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

  • —“Covered Service” means the specific software applications, cloud infrastructure, IoT platforms, and related technical solutions designated as covered by this SLA in the applicable Order Form or SOW.
  • —“Uptime” means the percentage of time in a calendar month that the Covered Service is accessible and functional via the public internet, calculated in accordance with Section 3, and excluding Scheduled Maintenance and Exclusions (Section 7).
  • —“Downtime” means any continuous period of five (5) or more consecutive minutes during which the Covered Service is unavailable (i.e., returns HTTP 5xx errors or fails to respond to valid API requests) as measured by our monitoring systems. Periods of less than five (5) consecutive minutes shall not be counted as Downtime.
  • —“Monthly Uptime Percentage” means the total number of minutes in a calendar month minus the number of minutes of Downtime suffered in that calendar month, divided by the total number of minutes in that calendar month, multiplied by 100. The formula is: ((Total Minutes − Downtime Minutes) ÷ Total Minutes) × 100.
  • —“Scheduled Maintenance” means planned periods of service unavailability notified to the Client at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance.
  • —“Service Credit” means a percentage of the monthly service fee credited to the Client as the sole remedy for failure to meet the Uptime Guarantee, calculated in accordance with Section 5.

3. Uptime Guarantee

Versa Morph commits that each Covered Service will achieve at least the following Uptime percentages during each calendar month (“Uptime Guarantee”):

Service Tier Monthly Uptime Guarantee Annual Uptime Target
Enterprise 99.95% 99.99%
Standard 99.9% 99.95%
Development / Staging 99.5% 99.8%

The Uptime Guarantee applies exclusively to cloud-hosted production services managed directly by Versa Morph. For on-premise, hybrid, or client-managed deployments, uptime is subject to the Client's infrastructure, security practices, and maintenance procedures, and no Uptime Guarantee is provided unless expressly agreed in a separate SOW.

4. Support Response Times

Versa Morph provides technical support for Covered Services in accordance with the severity classifications and response time commitments set forth below. Response times are measured from the moment a complete support ticket is submitted via our designated support channels (as defined in Section 11) and acknowledged by our support team.

Severity Definition Initial Response Time Coverage
Critical (P1) Complete service outage affecting all users. Data loss or confirmed security breach. Production system is down or unavailable. ≤ 30 minutes 24/7
High (P2) Major feature degradation affecting a significant subset of users. No reasonable workaround available. Performance severely degraded. ≤ 2 hours 24/7
Normal (P3) Partial non-critical feature degradation with a functional workaround. Non-critical bugs. Minor performance issues. ≤ 8 business hours Business hours
Low (P4) Cosmetic issues, general questions, feature requests, documentation errors, minor bugs with no impact on functionality. ≤ 48 business hours Business hours

Business hours are defined as Monday through Friday, 09:00 to 18:00 Western Indonesia Time (WIB, UTC+7), excluding Indonesian national public holidays. P1 and P2 incidents receive 24/7 coverage, including weekends and public holidays. “Initial Response” means our first substantive communication acknowledging the ticket, assessing severity, and deploying initial resources. Resolution time will vary based on the nature and complexity of the incident; we will use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve all incidents promptly.

5. Service Credits

If Versa Morph fails to meet the Monthly Uptime Guarantee for a Covered Service in a given calendar month, the Client shall be eligible to request Service Credits as follows. Service Credits are calculated based on the actual Monthly Uptime Percentage achieved:

Monthly Uptime Percentage Service Credit (% of Monthly Fee) Max Downtime (30-day month)
99.0% to <99.9% 5% ~7.2 hours
95.0% to <99.0% 10% ~36 hours
<95.0% 25% >36 hours

Service Credits are applied as deductions to future invoices issued after the credit is approved. The maximum total Service Credit awarded in any single calendar month shall not exceed 25% of the monthly service fee for the affected Covered Service. Service Credits are the Client's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure by Versa Morph to meet the Uptime Guarantee.

6. Credit Request Procedure

To request Service Credits, the Client must submit a written request to Versa Morph via the support channels specified in Section 11 within thirty (30) calendar days of the end of the calendar month in which the Downtime occurred. The request must include:

  • —A description of the Downtime incident(s), including dates, times (in WIB/UTC+7), and duration.
  • —Any available supporting evidence, such as monitoring reports, error logs, or correspondence.
  • —The Monthly Uptime Percentage as calculated by the Client and the corresponding Service Credit claimed.

Versa Morph will review and respond to the credit request within fifteen (15) business days of receipt. Versa Morph may request additional information to verify the Downtime. Failure to submit a timely and complete request may result in forfeiture of the Service Credit. Credits are not redeemable for cash and will not be paid as refunds.

7. Exclusions

The Uptime Guarantee and Service Credits shall not apply to any Downtime, unavailability, or performance degradation caused by any of the following (“Exclusions”):

  • —Scheduled Maintenance performed with at least forty-eight (48) hours advance notice via email or status page notification.
  • —Emergency maintenance required to address an immediate security vulnerability or critical system defect (notice given as soon as practicable).
  • —Actions or inactions by the Client or any of the Client's employees, contractors, or agents, including but not limited to changes to configurations, misuse of the Services, or failure to follow documented guidelines.
  • —Failures of third-party services, networks, cloud providers, or upstream infrastructure not under Versa Morph's direct control.
  • —Force majeure events as defined in the MSA, including but not limited to natural disasters, war, terrorism, civil unrest, fire, flood, earthquake, pandemic, cyberattacks (including DDoS attacks targeting the Client), and government actions.
  • —Beta, alpha, trial, or pre-release features explicitly labeled as “non-production,” “preview,” or “experimental.”
  • —Compliance or legal requirements that necessitate service modification, restriction, or suspension.
  • —Downtime during any period in which the Client's account is delinquent on payment.

8. Reporting & Verification

Versa Morph will provide monthly availability reports for each Covered Service upon the Client's written request. Clients may also monitor service availability using independent third-party monitoring tools at their own expense.

In the event of a dispute regarding Uptime calculations or the occurrence of Downtime, the parties agree to use Versa Morph's monitoring systems as the primary source of truth. If the Client disputes the accuracy of our monitoring data, the parties shall mutually agree upon an independent third-party monitoring service to serve as the definitive source of truth. The cost of such third-party verification shall be borne by the party that ultimately prevails in the dispute.

9. Scheduled Maintenance

Versa Morph will perform scheduled maintenance during designated maintenance windows. We will use commercially reasonable efforts to:

  • —Schedule maintenance during off-peak hours (as defined in the applicable SOW).
  • —Provide at least forty-eight (48) hours advance notice via email and our status page.
  • —Keep maintenance windows to the minimum duration necessary, not to exceed four (4) hours.
  • —Design maintenance procedures to be zero-downtime or minimally disruptive wherever technically feasible.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Versa Morph may perform emergency maintenance at any time without prior notice if necessary to protect the security, integrity, or availability of the Services.

10. Governing Law

This SLA shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Indonesia, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Any disputes arising under this SLA shall be resolved in accordance with the dispute resolution provisions set forth in the MSA.

11. Contact & Escalation

For technical support, to report a service incident, or to request Service Credits, the Client may contact Versa Morph through the following designated support channels:

  • —Support Email: hello@versamorph.id (all severity levels)
  • —P1 Emergency Hotline: Available 24/7/365 via the dedicated emergency contact number provided in your MSA or onboarding documentation.
  • —Status Page: For real-time service status and incident updates, please refer to our status page at https://versamorph.id/status (or as notified in your MSA).

This SLA is incorporated by reference into the Master Service Agreement between Versa Morph and the Client. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this SLA shall have the meanings given to them in the MSA. In the event of any conflict between the terms of this SLA and the MSA, the terms of the MSA shall prevail.

1. Definitions & Interpretation

  • —“Processing” means any operation or set of operations performed on Personal Data, whether or not by automated means, including collection, recording, organization, structuring, storage, adaptation, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure, dissemination, erasure, or destruction.

2. Processing of Personal Data

The Processor does not acquire any right, title, or interest in or to the Personal Data, except the limited right to Process such data strictly in accordance with this DPA.

The Processor shall not: (a) Process Personal Data for its own purposes; (b) sell Personal Data (as defined under the CCPA); or (c) retain, use, or disclose Personal Data outside the terms of this DPA.

2.3 Scope of Processing. The subject-matter, duration, nature, and purpose of the Processing, as well as the types of Personal Data and categories of Data Subjects, are set forth below:

  • —Categories of Data Subjects: The Controller's employees, contractors, customers, partners, vendors, and end-users whose Personal Data is processed by the Controller through the Services.

2.4 Additional Instructions. If the Processor reasonably believes that an instruction from the Controller violates Applicable Data Protection Laws, it shall promptly inform the Controller without delay and may refrain from executing the instruction until the Controller confirms or modifies it in writing.

3. Obligations of the Processor
