  • —Process Personal Data only on documented instructions from the Controller, unless required otherwise by EU, UK, Indonesian, or Member State law to which the Processor is subject. Where such law requires Processing, the Processor shall inform the Controller of that legal requirement before Processing, unless that law prohibits such information on important grounds of public interest.
  • —Ensure that persons authorized to Process the Personal Data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality.
  • —Implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational security measures as set forth in Section 6.
  • —Notify the Controller without undue delay (and in any event within 24 hours of confirmation) upon becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting the Controller's Personal Data.
  • —Assist the Controller by appropriate technical and organizational measures, insofar as this is possible, for the fulfillment of the Controller's obligation to respond to requests for exercising the Data Subject's rights.
  • —Assist the Controller in ensuring compliance with its obligations under Articles 32 to 36 of the GDPR (security, breach notification, data protection impact assessments, and prior consultation) taking into account the nature of the Processing and the information available to the Processor.
  • —At the Controller's choice, delete or return all Personal Data to the Controller after the end of the provision of Services, and delete existing copies unless storage is required by applicable law.
  • —Make available to the Controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with this DPA and allow for and contribute to audits and inspections as described in Section 10.

4. Subprocessors

4.1 Authorized Subprocessors. The Controller provides general written authorization for Versa Morph to engage the following Subprocessors for the provision of the Services. Versa Morph shall ensure that each Subprocessor is bound by a written data processing agreement that imposes data protection terms at least as restrictive as those set forth in this DPA:

Subprocessor Service Provided Data Processing Location SCCs in Place
Amazon Web Services (AWS) Cloud infrastructure (compute, storage, database, CDN) ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) Yes
Vercel Inc. Web application hosting, deployment, edge functions Global (multi-region, edge network) Yes
Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Data analytics, machine learning, IoT core, Kubernetes asia-southeast1 (Singapore) Yes

4.2 Engagement of New Subprocessors. Versa Morph shall notify the Controller at least thirty (30) calendar days before engaging any new Subprocessor (“Subprocessor Change Notice”). The Controller may object to the engagement of a new Subprocessor within fourteen (14) calendar days of receiving the Subprocessor Change Notice by providing a written objection explaining the reasonable grounds for such objection. If the Controller objects and Versa Morph cannot reasonably accommodate the objection within a commercially reasonable period, either party may terminate the affected portion of the Services without penalty.

5. Data Subject Rights

5.1 Versa Morph shall assist the Controller in fulfilling its obligations to respond to Data Subject requests under Applicable Data Protection Laws, including the rights of: access (GDPR Art. 15); rectification (Art. 16); erasure / “Right to be Forgotten” (Art. 17); restriction of processing (Art. 18); data portability (Art. 20); objection (Art. 21); and rights relating to automated decision-making (Art. 22).

5.2 If a Data Subject makes a request directly to Versa Morph, we shall promptly (and in any event within five (5) business days) forward the request to the Controller, together with any relevant information we hold that may assist in responding. Versa Morph shall not respond to the request without the Controller's prior written authorization, except where required by applicable law.

5.3 The Processor shall provide the Controller with self-service tools, APIs, and dashboards (where available) to enable the Controller to directly access, rectify, export, or delete Personal Data without requiring administrative intervention from the Processor.

6. Technical & Organizational Security Measures

Versa Morph maintains a comprehensive information security program designed to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Personal Data. The program is aligned with the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II control frameworks. Key security measures include, at a minimum:

  • —Encryption: Personal Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 or equivalent industry-standard encryption. Data in transit is protected using TLS 1.3 (or higher) for all network communications. Encryption keys are managed using a hardware security module (HSM) and rotated at least annually.
  • —Access Control: Access to Personal Data is restricted on a strict need-to-know basis using role-based access control (RBAC), multi-factor authentication (MFA), and the principle of least privilege. Access rights are reviewed and recertified on a quarterly basis. All access to Personal Data is logged and subject to audit.
  • —Network Security: Zero Trust architecture with micro-segmentation, next-generation firewalls (NGFW), web application firewall (WAF), DDoS protection, intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS), and 24/7 security operations center (SOC) monitoring.
  • —Vulnerability Management: Automated vulnerability scanning is conducted weekly across all production systems. Third-party penetration testing is performed at least annually by an independent, accredited security firm. A formal patch management policy requires critical-severity patches to be applied within 72 hours.
  • —Data Minimization & Pseudonymization: Where feasible, Personal Data is pseudonymized or anonymized to reduce the risk associated with Processing. The Processor collects and retains only the minimum Personal Data necessary to achieve the Processing purpose.
  • —Business Continuity: The Processor maintains a Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) plan with defined RPO/RTO targets. Production data is backed up daily with cross-region replication. Full DR testing is conducted at least annually.
  • —Personnel Security: All Processor personnel with access to Personal Data undergo mandatory security and privacy awareness training upon hire and annually thereafter. All personnel are bound by written confidentiality agreements. Background checks are conducted to the extent permitted by applicable law.

The Processor shall update its security measures as necessary to maintain an appropriate level of security, provided that such updates do not materially reduce the level of protection afforded to Personal Data.

7. Personal Data Breach Notification

7.1 Versa Morph shall notify the Controller without undue delay (and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours of confirmation) upon becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting the Controller's Personal Data. “Personal Data Breach” means a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of, or access to, Personal Data transmitted, stored, or otherwise processed by the Processor.

7.2 The notification shall include, to the extent available at the time:

  • —A description of the nature of the Personal Data Breach, including, where possible, the categories and approximate number of Data Subjects and Personal Data records concerned.
  • —The name and contact details of the Processor's Data Protection Officer or other security contact from whom further information may be obtained.
  • —A description of the likely consequences of the Personal Data Breach.
  • —A description of the measures taken or proposed to be taken to address the Personal Data Breach, including, where appropriate, measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects.

7.3 To the extent such information is not available at the time of the initial notification, the Processor shall provide it in phases as it becomes available, without further undue delay.

7.4 Versa Morph shall cooperate fully with the Controller in investigating and remediating the Personal Data Breach, including providing timely access to relevant logs, system data, forensic analysis, and personnel as reasonably required, and shall not take any action that would impede the Controller's ability to comply with its own breach notification obligations under Applicable Data Protection Laws.

8. Data Deletion & Return

8.1 Upon termination or expiry of the Services, or upon the Controller's written request at any time, Versa Morph shall, at the Controller's option, either: (a) return a complete copy of all Personal Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format (e.g., CSV, JSON); or (b) securely delete all Personal Data in its possession or control, including from all systems, backups, and disaster recovery media.

8.2 Versa Morph shall certify in writing within thirty (30) calendar days of completion that the deletion has been carried out in accordance with this Section 8. Such certification shall specify the date and method of deletion and the systems from which Personal Data was deleted.

8.3 Notwithstanding the foregoing, Versa Morph may retain Personal Data to the extent required by applicable law (including tax, anti-money laundering, and record-keeping obligations), provided that such retained Personal Data remains subject to the confidentiality and security obligations of this DPA and is processed solely for the purpose of compliance with such legal obligations.

9. International Data Transfers & Standard Contractual Clauses

9.1 Versa Morph is based in Indonesia and primarily processes Personal Data in the Asia Pacific region. Where the Processing of Personal Data involves a transfer of Personal Data from the European Economic Area (“EEA”), the United Kingdom, or Switzerland to a country that has not been deemed adequate by the European Commission, the UK Secretary of State, or the Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (as applicable), the parties agree that the transfer shall be governed by the Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as adopted by the European Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 of 4 June 2021 (Module Two: Controller to Processor), which are hereby incorporated by reference.

9.2 For transfers subject to the UK GDPR, the SCCs shall be supplemented by the UK International Data Transfer Addendum (Version B1.0) issued by the UK Information Commissioner's Office, which is hereby incorporated by reference.

9.3 Where SCCs apply, the following additional terms shall apply:

  • —Clause 7 (Docking Clause): Not included.
  • —Clause 9 (Use of Subprocessors): Option 2 (General written authorization), with a thirty (30) day prior notice period for changes.
  • —Clause 11 (Redress): The optional independent dispute resolution clause shall not apply.
  • —Clause 13 (Supervision): The supervisory authority of the EEA Member State in which the Controller is established shall be competent.
  • —Annexes: Annex I (Parties, Description of Transfer, Competent Supervisory Authority) and Annex II (Technical and Organizational Security Measures) are set forth in the MSA and this DPA.

9.4 To the extent required, the Controller hereby authorizes Versa Morph to execute any SCCs on behalf of the Controller as data exporter for the purposes of giving full effect to the SCCs. The Controller agrees to provide promptly any information reasonably requested by Versa Morph to facilitate the execution of SCCs.

10. Audit Rights

10.1 Upon thirty (30) calendar days' advance written notice, and no more than once per calendar year (unless a Personal Data Breach has occurred), the Controller (or its authorized representatives) may audit Versa Morph's compliance with this DPA. Audits shall be conducted during the Processor's regular business hours, at the Controller's sole expense, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt the Processor's operations.

10.2 Alternatively, and in satisfaction of the Controller's audit rights under this Section 10, Versa Morph may provide the Controller with: (a) a copy of its most recent SOC 2 Type II report; (b) a copy of its ISO 27001 certificate (if maintained); and/or (c) a summary of the results of its most recent penetration test. If the Controller reasonably determines that the provided documentation is insufficient to demonstrate compliance, the Controller may exercise its physical audit right under Section 10.1.

10.3 The Controller shall treat any information acquired during an audit as Confidential Information under the MSA and shall not disclose audit findings to any third party without the Processor's prior written consent, except as required by law.

11. Liability & Indemnification

11.1 Each party's liability for any breach of this DPA shall be subject to the limitations of liability set forth in the MSA. To the extent that a data protection authority assesses a fine or penalty against the Controller that arises from a breach by the Processor of its obligations under this DPA or Applicable Data Protection Laws, the Processor shall indemnify the Controller for the amount of such fine or penalty attributable to the Processor's breach.

11.2 Nothing in this DPA shall limit or exclude the liability of either party for: (a) death or personal injury caused by its negligence; (b) fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation; or (c) any other liability that cannot be limited or excluded under applicable law.

12. Governing Law & Execution

12.1 This DPA shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Indonesia, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. The GDPR shall apply to the Processing of Personal Data of Data Subjects in the European Union, and the UK GDPR shall apply to the Processing of Personal Data of Data Subjects in the United Kingdom, in each case to the extent required by Applicable Data Protection Laws.

12.2 Any disputes arising out of or in connection with this DPA shall be resolved in accordance with the dispute resolution provisions set forth in the MSA.

12.3 This DPA is effective as of the date the MSA is signed by both parties, unless a later date is specified in the MSA. This DPA may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.

12.4 To execute this DPA, please contact our team. A signed copy will be provided as an addendum to your Master Service Agreement.

legalPages.title: Non-Disclosure Agreement
legalPages.subtitle: This Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) governs the treatment of confidential information exchanged between Versa Morph and our partners, affiliates, or clients.
legalPages.content:
1. Purpose & Mutual Disclosure

This Non-Disclosure Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into by and between Versa Morph (“Company”) and the submitting party (“Partner,” “Affiliate,” or “User”) to protect proprietary data exchanged during project discovery, system estimation, and client referral interactions. Both parties agree that the sharing of confidential business details is necessary to evaluate collaborative scopes and arichitecture designs.

2. Definition of Confidential Information

“Confidential Information” refers to any proprietary, non-public data, materials, or information disclosed by either party (directly or indirectly), whether written, oral, or visual. This includes, but is not limited to:

  • •Project Documentation: Project briefs, Terms of Reference (TOR), RFPs, pricing structures, arichitecture diagrams, and workflow blueprints.
  • •Client Details: Customer listings, client PIC contact details, lead temperature metrics, and contract scopes.
  • •Technical Assets: Source code, system integrations, database schemas, and proprietary hardware designs.

3. Non-Disclosure & Restricted Use Covenants

Both parties agree to protect all Confidential Information with the same degree of care they use to safeguard their own highly sensitive data (but no less than a reasonable standard of care). Obligations include:

  • •Information must be used solely to evaluate potential development scopes or manage referral negotiations.
  • •Information must not be copied, reverse-engineered, or distributed without prior written authorization.
  • •Physical and digital files must be stored in secure, encrypted environments to prevent leaks.

4. Permitted Disclosures & Need-to-Know

Access to Confidential Information must be restricted strictly to employees, contractors, or professional advisors who require access to evaluate the referral. The receiving party must ensure that all such individuals are bound by written confidentiality agreements at least as restrictive as this Agreement.

5. Compelled Disclosures

If the receiving party is required by law, regulation, or court order to disclose any portion of the Confidential Information, they must: (a) provide the disclosing party with prompt written notice to allow them to seek a protective order; (b) cooperate fully in any efforts to limit disclosure; and (c) disclose only that portion of the information that is legally mandated.

6. Exclusions from Confidential Treatment

Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly known through no breach of this Agreement; (b) is already lawfully in the receiving party's possession prior to disclosure; (c) is independently developed by the receiving party without reference to the disclosing party's data; or (d) is lawfully obtained from a third party without confidentiality constraints.

7. Term & Return of Materials

The non-disclosure obligations set forth herein shall commence upon form submission and remain in effect for a period of five (5) years from the date of disclosure. Upon written request, the receiving party must promptly return or destroy all physical and digital copies of the Confidential Information and provide written certification of such destruction.

8. Intellectual Property & Licensing

This Agreement does not grant or imply any transfer of ownership, license, or right over the disclosing party's Background IP, patents, copyrights, or trademarks. All disclosed files and materials remain the sole property of their respective owner.

9. Breach, Remedies & Governing Law

A breach of this Agreement may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages alone would be inadequate. Consequently, the disclosing party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief, specific performance, and other equitable remedies, in addition to recovering reasonable legal fees.

This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Indonesia. Any unresolved dispute shall be finally settled by arbitration administered by BANI in Jakarta, Indonesia.

legalPages.subtitle: This Affiliate Partner Agreement governs your participation in the Versa Morph Growth Partner Program. Please review these terms in full before registering.
legalPages.content:
1. Enrollment & Eligibility

By registering for the Versa Morph Affiliate Partner Program, you represent and warrant that: (a) you have the full legal capacity and authority to enter into this Agreement; (b) all registration details provided (including full legal name, contact email, phone number, and professional affiliations) are accurate, complete, and current; and (c) your participation does not violate any third-party contracts or legal obligations.

Versa Morph reserves the absolute right to audit all affiliate applications and verify professional credentials. We may decline or terminate any affiliate account at our sole discretion if we identify spamming, self-referral schemes, duplicate registrations, or the submission of low-quality or fraudulent leads.

2. Referral Mechanics & Cookies

To ensure accurate tracking and commission allocation, you must adhere to the following mechanisms:

2.1 Tracked Leads Requirements

  • •Project Submission Form: Referrals must be submitted through the official project referral page at /affiliate/submit-project with your unique Affiliate ID pre-filled or entered.
  • •Calculator Referrals: Client estimates computed via the interactive Project Calculator at /calculator containing your referral query parameter (`?ref=YOUR_ID`) will set a tracking cookie on the user's device.
  • •Cookie Validity: Referral cookies are valid for a duration of ninety (90) days. If the client submits a contact request using the same browser during this period, the conversion will be credited to you.

2.2 Lead Exclusions

Referral commission will not be awarded for: (a) clients already recorded in Versa Morph's active CRM system or engaged in active sales negotiations within the preceding six (6) months; (b) self-referrals, where you hold direct ownership, executive positions, or employment at the referred entity; and (c) leads submitted without a valid Affiliate ID before contract execution.

3. Commission Calculations

Commissions are calculated as a percentage of the Net Contract Value of the referred project:

  • •Net Contract Value: Refers to the total professional service fee agreed upon in the signed Statement of Work (SOW), excluding value-added tax (PPN), government levies, third-party software licenses, cloud infrastructure hosting fees, and hardware telemetry procurement costs.
  • •Standard Commission Rate: Ranges from 5% to 10% of the Net Contract Value. The final commission rate is evaluated based on project complexity and approved by the Versa Morph business development desk prior to client signing.
  • •Adjustment Rights: We reserve the right to modify commission rates for enterprise accounts requiring custom pricing structures or volume discounts. Such modifications will be agreed upon with the affiliate in writing.

4. Payout Milestones & Taxes

To maintain healthy cash flow and align with project delivery milestones, payouts are distributed as follows:

4.1 Pro-Rata Payment Milestones

Commission is released progressively following the payment schedule agreed upon with the client. For example, if a project is split into a 40% deposit, 40% mid-point milestone, and 20% final delivery milestone, your commission will be released in matching 40%, 40%, and 20% increments as the client payments clear.

4.2 Processing and Tax Obligations

  • •Payout Window: All milestone commissions are paid to the affiliate within seven (7) business days after the corresponding client invoice is fully paid and the funds have cleared in our bank accounts.
  • •Tax Withholding: Payouts are subject to tax withholding under Indonesian tax regulations (PPh 21 for individuals or PPh 23 for corporate entities). Affiliates must submit a valid NPWP (tax identification number) to ensure correct tax processing. Otherwise, a higher withholding rate may apply.

5. Marketing Rules & Restrictions

Affiliates must represent Versa Morph professionally. You agree to comply with the following marketing guidelines:

  • •No Keyword Bidding: You may not bid on search engine keywords containing trademarked terms such as “Versa Morph,” “versamorph.id,” or close variations in PPC campaigns.
  • •No Domain Squatting: You are prohibited from registering domains, social media handles, or search channels using the trademarked name “Versa Morph”.
  • •Anti-Spam: You must not send unsolicited bulk emails (spam), post automated referral comments on forums, or use deceptive redirects to drive traffic to our estimator.

6. Confidentiality & IP Rights

Affiliates will have access to sensitive client project briefs, RFP attachments, and corporate pricing. You agree to protect this information as Confidential Information and not disclose it to any third parties without prior written consent.

Participation in this program does not grant you any ownership or licensing rights over Versa Morph's Background IP, brand logos, codebases, or copyrighted assets. You may only use our approved brand logos in promotional channels as expressly authorized by our marketing guidelines.

7. Independent Contractor Status

The relationship between you and Versa Morph is strictly that of an Independent Contractor. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to create a partnership, joint venture, agency, franchise, or employment relationship.

You are solely responsible for declaring and paying your own income taxes, social security contributions, and business expenses incurred during the execution of your referral activities. You are not authorized to negotiate contracts, sign documents, or bind Versa Morph legally in any capacity.

8. Term, Termination & Settlement

This Agreement commences upon registration and continues until terminated. Either party may terminate this Agreement at any time, for convenience or cause, by giving seven (7) days' written notice to the other party.

Upon termination: (a) you must immediately remove all promotional links and brand materials from your channels; and (b) any active referrals logged and approved prior to the termination date will remain eligible for commission payouts upon client payment clearance.

9. Indemnification & Dispute Resolution

You agree to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Versa Morph and its officers from any third-party claims, losses, liabilities, or legal expenses arising out of your breach of this Agreement, deceptive marketing practices, or violation of applicable data privacy laws.

This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Indonesia. Any dispute arising from this kemitraan shall first be referred to mediation. If mediation fails within sixty (60) days, the dispute shall be finally settled by arbitration administered by BANI in Jakarta, Indonesia.

legalPages.titleHtml: Applicant Privacy Consent
legalPages.subtitle: This document describes how Versa Morph manages applicant profiles, CVs, and credentials during recruitment processes.
legalPages.content:
1. Identity of Controller

Recruitment applications and candidate data submitted through the Careers portal are controlled by Versa Morph, a company registered under the laws of the Republic of Indonesia with its office at Jl. M.H. Thamrin No. 1, Jakarta Pusat, DKI Jakarta 10310, Indonesia. Versa Morph acts as the primary data controller for the processing of applicant records.

2. Recruitment Data We Collect

We collect candidate details including: (a) contact details (full name, email address, phone number); (b) credentials (resumes, CV attachments, cover letters, and work portfolios); (c) professional profiles (LinkedIn or GitHub); and (d) expected salary ranges and earliest start dates.

3. Purposes & Legal Basis

Candidate data is processed under the following legal bases:

  • •Pre-Contractual Steps (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)): Assessing qualifications and suitability for employment positions.
  • •Consent (GDPR Art. 6(1)(a)): Voluntarily opt-in choices for reference checks, automated testing scheduling, and communications.
  • •Legitimate Interests: Verifying academic records, professional licenses, and conducting candidate screening.

4. Candidate Data Retention

Successful candidate files will form part of the official employee profile. Unsuccessful applications are retained for up to two (2) years to consider candidates for future opportunities. Candidates may request deletion of their files at any time.

5. Third-Party Sharing & Security

Candidate data is stored securely and accessed only by hiring managers and HR personnel. We do not sell or license resume files to marketing platforms. We may utilize verified screening tools bound by strict data processing covenants.

6. Security & Telemetry

All resumes and CV uploads are encrypted using AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit. System logs tracking applicant submissions record IP addresses and timestamps, retained for a maximum of twelve (12) months for security monitoring.

7. Candidate Data Rights

Under Indonesian Personal Data Protection (UU PDP) and global privacy rules, you possess the right to: (a) view all candidate records we hold about you; (b) correct errors in your profile; (c) request deletion of your CV and attachments; or (d) withdraw your recruitment consent at any stage of the application by contacting our recruiting desk.

8. Recruitment DPO Contact

For inquiries or requests regarding candidate data protection, please contact the Data Protection Officer at: dpo@versamorph.id.
